ideas.name: ClipTrigger
ideas.problem: The massive time sink caused by manually scrubbing through multi-hour VODs to find high-engagement clips for social media platforms like TikTok and Reels.
ideas.targetUser: Mid-to-large scale Twitch/YouTube streamers and their freelance video editors who need to convert long-form broadcasts into high-velocity short-form content.
coreFeatures: Global Hotkey Tagging
Contextual Metadata Labels (e.g., 'Funny', 'Clutch', 'Fail')
Minimalist Streamer Overlay Dashboard
Instant Editor Export (JSON/CSV/Google Sheets)
OBS Status Syncing
realDependencies: OBS WebSocket API
AWS S3 for cloud log synchronization
Twitch/YouTube API for VOD metadata retrieval
Local SQLite database for offline logging
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will replace the OBS WebSocket with a simulated 'Stream Controller' service that uses a setInterval to mimic a running stream timer and 'Live' status. Cloud uploads will be simulated using a Promise that resolves after a random delay of 800ms to 2500ms to mimic network latency. All user 'tags' will be stored in a local state array that simulates a database, providing immediate UI feedback as if the data were being persisted to a remote server.

ideas.name: SlotFlow
ideas.problem: The 'Email/Spreadsheet Chaos'—creators lose track of sponsorship dates, missing creative assets, and managing diverse advertiser requirements across fragmented communication channels.
ideas.targetUser: Solo newsletter operators and small media teams (e.g., Substack/Beehiiv power users) managing 3+ sponsors per issue and experiencing high administrative overhead.
coreFeatures: Dynamic Inventory Calendar (Drag-and-drop sponsorship slot scheduling)
Advertiser Asset Portal (Secure, self-serve upload link for sponsors to provide copy/images)
Asset Status Pipeline (Visual tracking from 'Pending' to 'Approved' to 'Scheduled')
Automated Deadline Reminders (Automated notifications for approaching asset deadlines)
realDependencies: AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage for asset hosting
Postmark or SendGrid for automated advertiser communication
Auth0 for secure multi-tenant user authentication
Stripe API for managing sponsorship payments
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a centralized local state object to act as a mock database. All 'API calls' will be wrapped in a delay function using Math.random() to simulate network latency. File uploads will be faked using URL.createObjectURL for local files to mimic S3 storage. Email notifications will be simulated by updating an 'Internal System Log' UI component within the app to show 'Email sent to [address]' rather than hitting an actual SMTP server.

ideas.name: LumeCheck
ideas.problem: Inconsistent material behavior and 'material breaking' when assets are moved from DCC tools to various game engines under non-standard lighting conditions.
ideas.targetUser: Environment Artists and Technical Artists in game production pipelines who need to ensure PBR (Physically Based Rendering) accuracy across different engine environments.
coreFeatures: Instant Environment Preset Switching (e.g., Golden Hour, Neon Night, Overcast, Studio High-Key)
PBR Integrity Heatmap (visualizes roughness and metallic map deviations under specific light)
Cross-Engine Shader Emulation (side-by-side comparison of Unreal Engine 5 vs Unity HDRP look)
Batch Consistency Audit (generates a pass/fail report for entire asset libraries based on lighting thresholds)
realDependencies: WebGL or WebGPU-based real-time rendering engine
glTF/USD asset parsing and loading library
Compute shaders for real-time PBR error calculation
Cloud-based high-fidelity ray-tracing API for heavy assets
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will simulate heavy computational loads by introducing a 3-5 second 'Analyzing Material' progress bar using async/await. Real-time 3D rendering will be faked by swapping between 4 high-resolution pre-rendered 360-degree environment spheres and applying CSS filters to a static 3D model placeholder to mimic lighting shifts. The 'PBR Heatmap' will be an overlay of a pre-made red/green gradient texture that changes based on the selected preset. The 'Batch Audit' will generate a randomized but structured JSON report with plausible error percentages to simulate data processing.

ideas.name: LinkBound
ideas.niche: Indie Game Asset Dependency & Version Auditing
ideas.problem: Broken prefab references, lost asset links, and version mismatches caused by rapid asset iterations in Unity and Godot, leading to 'pink textures' and missing component errors.
ideas.targetUser: Solo indie developers and small technical art teams managing high-asset-count projects who frequently face workflow-breaking reference errors during rapid development cycles.
coreFeatures: Interactive Visual Dependency Graph
Impact Analysis Simulator (What-if Scenarios)
Automated Orphan Asset Detection
Real-time Version Drift Alerts
realDependencies: Unity/Godot Editor Plugin APIs
Version Control System APIs (Git/LFS/Perforce)
Local File System Watcher
Graph Database (Neo4j) for relational mapping
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'Project Manifest' JSON file that mimics a complex folder structure with hardcoded GUIDs and file paths. Instead of real-time engine polling, an asynchronous 'MockEngineService' will return this data via Promises with randomized delays (400ms–1500ms) to simulate disk I/O. A 'Simulate Breakage' button will allow the user to manually toggle a 'broken' state in the mock data, triggering the UI's alert and graph-red-lining logic as if a real file reference had been lost.

ideas.name: BrushFlow
ideas.problem: Fragmented communication across Discord, Twitter, and Email causing 'client creep,' lost feedback, and unmanaged revision rounds.
ideas.targetUser: Freelance digital illustrators and concept artists (primarily ages 18-35) who manage high-volume social media commissions and struggle with scope creep.
coreFeatures: Structured Briefing Engine: Dynamic client forms to capture references, color palettes, and usage rights upfront.
Visual Feedback Canvas: A WIP (Work-In-Progress) stage where clients can drop 'pins' and comments directly onto specific areas of an uploaded sketch or lineart.
Revision Guard: A built-in counter that tracks agreed-upon revision rounds and automatically flags 'out-of-scope' requests for additional billing.
Milestone Payment Tracker: A dashboard to monitor deposit status, progress payments, and final balance triggers.
realDependencies: Stripe API for payment processing and escrow-style deposits
AWS S3 or Cloudinary for high-resolution image hosting and versioning
Firebase Auth for secure artist and client login synchronization
SendGrid API for automated email notifications when a new WIP is ready for review
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest containing 'dummy' clients, commission statuses, and Unsplash image URLs. A MockService class will wrap all data calls, using 'setTimeout' to simulate 800ms-1500ms of network latency to mimic real API calls. Payment success will be simulated with a 90% probability of a 'Success' response from a fake Stripe handler. Visual feedback 'pins' will be stored in local state as coordinate objects {x, y, comment} to demonstrate functionality without a live database.
